english: The offences of the ancestors, undeserving, you will pay for,
note: lues: future of luo, 'atone for, pay the penalty of'. maiorum: of the forefathers.

english: Roman, until you have rebuilt the temples
note: refeceris: future perfect.

english: and the falling shrines of the gods and
note: aedis = aedes (accusative plural); labentis = labentes.

english: the images foul with black smoke.

latin: dis te minorem quod geris, imperas:
english: Because you bear yourself lesser than the gods, you rule:
note: dis te minorem ... geris: 'you conduct yourself as inferior to the gods'.

latin: hinc omne principium, huc refer exitum:
english: from here every beginning; to here refer the outcome:
note: hinc ... huc: from the gods, to the gods.

english: the gods, neglected, have given many
evils to mournful Hesperia.
note: Hesperia: Italy, the western land.

latin: iam bis Monaeses et Pacori manus
english: Already twice Monaeses and the band of Pacorus
note: Monaeses and Pacorus: Parthian commanders who defeated Roman armies (40 and 36 BC).

english: has crushed the unauspicious onsets
note: contudit: singular verb with the compound subject. inauspicatos: undertaken without (favourable) auspices.

english: our, and to have added the plunder
note: nostros agrees with impetus (line 10): 'our onsets'.

english: to their meagre neck-chains beams.
note: renidet: singular, the Parthian (band) beams with pleasure; 'their' supplied. torques: neck-chains, Parthian ornaments, enriched with Roman spoil.

english: Almost, occupied with seditions,
note: paene goes with delevit (line 14); occupatam agrees with urbem (line 14). seditionibus: the civil wars.

english: the Dacian and the Ethiopian destroyed the city,
note: Aethiops: the Egyptian (and Ethiopian) forces of Cleopatra at Actium; Dacus: the Dacians, allied with Antony.

english: this one dreaded for the fleet, that one
note: hic = the Aethiops (Egypt's fleet), ille = the Dacus.

english: better with missile arrows.
Generations fertile in sin marriages
note: culpae: genitive with fecunda. nuptias is the object of inquinavere (line 18).

latin: primum inquinavere et genus et domos:
english: first have defiled, both the stock and the homes:
note: inquinavere = inquinaverunt.

english: from this source drawn off, disaster
note: derivata: channelled off (a metaphor from water-channels).

english: into the fatherland and the people has flowed.
rejoices to be taught Ionic movements
note: motus Ionicos: Ionian (voluptuous) dance movements; the subject virgo is in line 22.

english: the ripe maiden, and is fashioned in arts
note: matura: of marriageable age. artibus: ablative 'by/in arts'; some take it as dative 'for arts'.

english: already now, and unchaste loves
from the tender nail she ponders.
note: de tenero ungui: 'from the tender nail', i.e. from earliest childhood (Greek ex hapalon onychon). meditatur: plans, dwells on.

english: Soon she seeks younger adulterers
note: iuniores: younger (than her husband).

english: amid the husband's wines, nor chooses
note: inter mariti vina: at her husband's drinking-parties.

english: to whom she may give unpermitted, hastily,
note: inpermissa agrees with gaudia (line 28).

english: joys, the lights having been removed,
note: luminibus remotis: ablative absolute, the lamps taken away.

latin: sed iussa coram non sine conscio
english: but, bidden, openly, not without the knowing
note: non sine conscio marito: with the husband privy to it; the negative is kept as it stands.

english: husband, she rises, whether a peddler calls
note: marito ends the phrase begun in line 29. institor: a travelling salesman, huckster.

english: or the master of a Spanish ship,
of disgraces a costly buyer.
note: pretiosus emptor: a buyer who pays a high price.

english: Not from these parents the youth sprung
dyed the sea with Punic blood
note: infecit: stained. Punic: Carthaginian (the First Punic War's sea battles).

english: and Pyrrhus and huge struck down
note: cecidit: from caedo, 'cut down, slew'.

english: Antiochus and dread Hannibal,
but of rustic soldiers the manly
offspring, taught with Sabellian mattocks
note: Sabellis: Sabine/Samnite, i.e. of the hardy Italian hill peoples.

english: to turn the clods and, of a strict
mother at the bidding, cut
note: recisos agrees with fustis (line 41).

english: to carry staves, when the sun, of the mountains,
note: montium: genitive with umbras on line 42, the shadows of the mountains

english: would shift the shadows and would take the yokes
note: mutaret, demeret: subjunctives in an iterative/descriptive temporal clause; kept as 'would'.

english: from the wearied oxen, a friendly
note: bubus = bobus, dative of separation.

english: time bringing on with departing chariot.
note: agens: the sun bringing on the welcome hour (evening); abeunte curru: ablative absolute, as its chariot departs.

english: What has ruinous day not impaired?
note: dies: time (literally 'day').

english: The age of parents, worse than grandfathers, has borne
note: avis: ablative of comparison, 'than (our) grandfathers'.

english: us more worthless, soon to give
an offspring more vicious.

latin: Quid fles, Asterie, quem tibi, candidi
english: Why do you weep, Asterie, for one whom to you the bright
note: quem: the antecedent is iuvenem Gygen (lines 4-5), object of fles. candidi: bright, clear-skied (agreeing with Favonii).

english: at the first of spring will restore, the Favonii,
note: Favonii: the west winds of spring. primo vere: at the beginning of spring.

english: with Thynian merchandise blessed,
note: Thyna: Bithynian. beatum: wealthy, enriched.

english: a young man of constant faith,
note: fide: archaic genitive (= fidei).

latin: Gygen? ille Notis actus ad Oricum
english: Gyges? He, driven by the Noti to Oricum
note: Noti: the south winds. Oricum: a port in Epirus.

english: after the mad stars of the She-goat, cold
note: Caprae sidera: the star Capella, whose rising (autumn) brings storms. frigidas agrees with noctis (line 7).

english: nights not without many
note: noctis = noctes; double negative non sine kept.

english: sleepless, tears, he passes.
note: insomnis may be accusative plural with noctis ('sleepless nights') or nominative with ille; the order is kept. lacrimis: with tears.

english: And yet the messenger of his anxious hostess,
note: hospitae: the woman entertaining him (Chloe); 'his' supplied.

english: that Chloe sighs and, wretched, with your
note: tuis agrees with ignibus (line 11): 'your fires', i.e. passion for your man (Gyges). Indirect statement after dicens (line 11).

english: saying, by fires is burned,
note: ignibus uri: is burned by fires, i.e. by passion (metaphor).

english: tempts him, crafty, in a thousand ways:
note: 'him' supplied; vafer: the crafty messenger.

english: how the faithless woman the credulous Proetus
note: mulier perfida: Anteia/Stheneboea, wife of Proetus. Subject mulier, object Proetum.

english: with false charges drove, too
note: inpulerit: perfect subjunctive, indirect question.

english: chaste Bellerophon
note: nimis casto: 'too chaste'; Bellerophontae: dative of disadvantage, '(death) for Bellerophon'.

english: to hasten death, he relates;
he tells of Peleus almost given to Tartarus,
note: Pelea: Greek accusative of Peleus.

english: while the Magnesian Hippolyte he flees, abstaining,
note: Hippolyte: wife of Acastus of Magnesia, who accused Peleus as Anteia accused Bellerophon. fugit: present, 'shuns'.

english: and, teaching to sin,
note: docentis = docentes, agreeing with historias (line 20).

english: the deceiver, stories brings up.
note: fallax: nominative, the deceitful messenger. movet: stirs up, tells.

english: In vain: for, deafer than the rocks of Icarus,
note: Icari: the island Icaria (Icarus), with dangerous cliffs.

latin: voces audit adhuc integer. at tibi
english: the words he hears, still untouched. But for you
note: integer: whole, untouched (still faithful).

english: lest neighbour Enipeus
more than right should please, beware;
note: plus iusto: more than is just.

latin: quamvis non alius flectere equum sciens
english: although no other, knowing how to turn a horse,
note: non alius: the negative kept where it stands.

english: equally is looked at on the Martian grass,
note: gramine Martio: the Campus Martius.

english: nor anyone, equally quick,
swims down the Tuscan channel.
note: Tusco alveo: the Tiber, which rises in Etruria.

latin: prima nocte domum claude neque in vias
english: At first nightfall shut the house, and do not into the streets
note: prima nocte: at the beginning of night.

english: at the song of the plaintive pipe look down,
and to him often calling you
note: vocanti: dative, the one calling you.

english: hard, difficult, remain.
note: duram: accusative agreeing with te (line 31), 'calling you hard'; difficilis: nominative, 'remain difficult'.

english: On the Martian Kalends, a bachelor, what I am doing,
note: Martiis kalendis: 1 March, the Matronalia, a festival for married women; hence the surprise that a bachelor (caelebs) celebrates. agam: subjunctive of indirect question.

latin: quid velint flores et acerra turis
english: what the flowers mean and the box of incense
note: acerra: an incense-box.

english: full, you wonder, and the charcoal placed on
living turf,
note: caespite vivo: an altar of fresh turf.

english: learned in the discourses of each tongue?
note: docte: vocative, addressed to Maecenas; sermones: accusative of respect. utriusque linguae: Greek and Latin.

english: I had vowed a sweet feast and a white
goat to Liber, nearly buried
note: Libero: Liber = Bacchus. funeratus: literally 'given a funeral', i.e. killed.

english: by the blow of a tree.
note: Horace's escape from a falling tree (cf. Odes 2.13).

english: This day, festive with the returning year,
note: anno redeunte: ablative absolute, the anniversary.

english: the cork bound with pitch will remove
note: corticem: bark-cork.

english: of a jar set to drink smoke
note: fumum bibere: wine was mellowed in a smoke-loft. institutae: set, placed.

english: with Tullus consul.
note: consule Tullo: a consulship of L. Volcacius Tullus (66 or 33 BC), dating the jar.

english: Take, Maecenas, ladles of your friend
note: cyathos: ladlefuls of wine, drunk 'to' or 'in honour of' the friend; amici sospitis: genitive, 'of your friend being safe'; 'your' supplied.

english: being safe, a hundred, and the wakeful lamps
note: centum agrees with cyathos.

latin: perfer in lucem: procul omnis esto
english: carry on into the light: far away let every
note: perfer in lucem: keep (them burning) through to daylight.

english: shout be, and anger.
note: esto: future imperative; its subject omnis clamor is split over lines 15-16.

english: Let go civic cares about the city:
note: mitte: let go, dismiss. civilis = civiles.

english: has fallen the column of the Dacian Cotiso,
note: occidit: perfect, 'has perished'. Cotiso: a Dacian king.

english: the Mede, hostile to himself, with mournful
note: Medus: the Parthian, in civil strife.

english: arms is at strife,
serves, of the Spanish coast the old enemy,
the Cantabrian, tamed by a late chain,
note: Cantaber: the Cantabrians of northern Spain.

english: now the Scythians, with slackened bow, plan
to withdraw from the plains.
note: campis: ablative of separation.

english: Neglectful, lest in any way the people may suffer,
note: neglegens ne qua ...: careless (about whether) anywhere the people be in trouble.

english: refrain, a private man, from too much caution, and
note: parce ... cavere: literally 'spare to be cautious', i.e. stop being too cautious; privatus: as a private citizen.

english: the gifts of the present hour take, glad,
leave grave things.
note: severa: neuter plural, serious matters.

english: “As long as I was pleasing to you
note: Speaker: the man (Horace). The poem is a dialogue in alternating stanzas; the source's quotation marks are not carried into the English.

english: and no one more preferred his arms round your white
note: potior: more favoured; bracchia ... dabat: was putting (his) arms around; 'his', 'round' and 'your' supplied.

english: neck, a young man, was putting,
note: iuvenis: nominative, in apposition with quisquam.

english: I flourished more blessed than the king of the Persians.”
note: rege: ablative of comparison.

english: “As long as for no other woman more
note: donec non alia: the negative kept where it stands; alia: ablative, 'for another woman'. Speaker: Lydia.

latin: arsisti neque erat Lydia post Chloen,
english: you burned, nor was Lydia after Chloe,
note: post Chloen: second to Chloe.

english: Lydia of much name,
note: multi nominis: genitive of quality, 'of great renown'.

english: I flourished more famous than Roman Ilia.”
note: Ilia: mother of Romulus and Remus.

english: “Me now Thracian Chloe rules,
note: Speaker: the man (Horace). Thressa: Thracian.

latin: dulcis docta modos et citharae sciens,
english: taught sweet measures and knowing of the lyre,
note: dulcis docta modos: taught sweet measures (accusative after a passive participle); citharae sciens: genitive with sciens.

english: for whom I shall not fear to die,
note: metuam: future (or present subjunctive).

english: if the fates will spare the soul, surviving.”
note: animae: Chloe, 'my life/soul' (term of endearment); superstiti: predicative, 'so that she survives'. The source lacks a final full stop.

english: “Me scorches with a mutual torch
note: Speaker: Lydia. face mutua: a torch of mutual love (metaphor).

english: Calais, son of Thurian Ornytus,
note: Thurini: of Thurii in southern Italy.

english: for whom twice I shall endure to die,
if the fates will spare the boy, surviving.”
note: superstiti: predicative, as in line 12.

english: “What if the former Venus returns
note: Speaker: the man (Horace). prisca Venus: the old love.

english: and those parted compels with a bronze yoke?
note: diductos: masculine plural, the two lovers parted; cogit: forces together.

english: if golden-haired Chloe is shaken out
note: excutitur: is thrown out (from the house).

english: and to rejected Lydia the door stands open?”
note: reiectae: dative, 'for Lydia, rejected'.

english: “Although more beautiful than a star
note: Speaker: Lydia.

latin: ille est, tu levior cortice et inprobo
english: he is, you lighter than cork and than the wanton
note: inprobo agrees with Hadria (line 23); 'than' supplied, ablatives of comparison.

english: more irascible than Hadria:
note: Hadria: the Adriatic sea.

latin: tecum vivere amem, tecum obeam lubens.”
english: with you I would love to live, with you I would die, willing.”
note: amem, obeam: potential subjunctives. lubens = libens.

english: If you drank the farthest Tanais, Lyce,
note: Tanain: the river Don; i.e. if you lived among the remotest Scythians. biberes: imperfect subjunctive, unreal condition.

latin: saevo nupta viro, me tamen asperas
english: wed to a savage husband, me nevertheless, to the rough
note: asperas agrees with Aquilonibus (line 4).

english: stretched out before the doors, to expose to the native
note: foris = fores (doors). incolis: dative, agreeing with Aquilonibus, 'native, dwelling there'.

english: you would lament, Aquilones.
note: plorares: you would be sorry. Aquilonibus: the north winds (dative with obicere). The source has no question mark or stop after this line.

latin: audis, quo strepitu ianua, quo nemus
english: Do you hear with what din the door, with what the grove
planted among the beautiful dwellings bellows back
note: nemus ... satum: a grove planted in the courtyard of a grand house.

latin: ventis et positas ut glaciet nives
english: to the winds, and how the settled snows freezes
note: ventis: to the winds (or ablative 'from the winds'). positas: laid down, fallen.

english: with clear divinity Jupiter?
note: puro numine: by his clear (cloudless) power; Jupiter as the sky.

english: Put aside haughtiness unwelcome to Venus,

latin: ne currente retro funis eat rota:
english: lest, with the wheel running back, the rope go:
note: metaphor from a windlass: if the wheel runs backward the rope goes with it, i.e. your pride may undo you.

english: not you as a Penelope difficult to suitors
note: Penelopen: Greek accusative, predicative with te.

english: did a Tyrrhenian parent beget.
note: Tyrrhenus: Etruscan; the Etruscans were reputedly loose-living.

latin: o quamvis neque te munera nec preces
english: O, although neither you gifts nor prayers
note: neque ... nec ... nec ... nec: the negatives kept as they stand; te is the object of curvat (line 16).

english: nor the pallor of lovers tinged with violet
note: tinctus viola: tinged with violet (pale-yellow) hue.

english: nor your husband, wounded by a Pierian mistress,
note: 'your' supplied. Pieria: Thessalian/Macedonian (or Muse-like, i.e. a skilled singer). saucius: wounded (by love, metaphor).

english: bends, your suppliants
note: curvat: bends (metaphor), i.e. moves you.

english: may you spare, neither softer than the rigid oak
note: parcas: jussive/optative subjunctive. nec ... nec: the negatives kept; describes Lyce. aesculo: winter-oak, ablative of comparison.

english: nor in mind gentler than Moorish snakes:
note: animum: accusative of respect.

latin: non hoc semper erit liminis aut aquae
english: not always will this, of threshold or water
note: non ... semper: negative kept where it stands. liminis, aquae: genitives with patiens (line 20).

english: from heaven enduring be, side.
note: caelestis agrees with aquae (rain). latus: 'side', i.e. my body (lying at your threshold).

english: Mercury, for with you as master, teachable,
note: te magistro: ablative absolute. docilis: Amphion, apt to learn.

english: Amphion moved the stones by singing,
note: Amphion built the walls of Thebes by his music.

english: and you, tortoise, to resound on seven
note: testudo: the tortoise-shell lyre. resonare: infinitive with callida (line 4).

english: skilled, strings,
note: nervis: on (its seven) strings.

latin: nec loquax olim neque grata, nunc et
english: neither talkative once nor pleasing, now both
note: nec ... neque: negatives kept.

english: to the tables of the rich and friendly to the temples,
tell measures to which Lyde her obstinate
note: 'her' supplied. obstinatas agrees with auris (line 8).

english: may apply ears,
note: auris = aures.

latin: quae velut latis equa trima campis
english: who, like a three-year mare on the wide plains,
note: trima: three years old.

english: plays bounding, and fears to be touched,
note: exsultim: with leaps.

english: without a share of marriages and still to a forward
note: expers: having no part in. protervo agrees with marito (line 12).

english: husband unripe.
note: cruda: unripe (metaphor), i.e. not yet ready for marriage.

english: You can tigers and woods as companions
lead and delay swift streams;
yielded, monstrous, to you as you coaxed,
note: immanis: nominative, agreeing with ianitor. blandienti: dative participle, 'to you charming'.

english: the doorkeeper of the hall,
note: aulae: the hall of the underworld.

english: Cerberus, although Fury-like a hundred
note: furiale: agrees with caput (line 18), like the Furies' (snake-wreathed). The authenticity of stanza 17-20 is doubted by some editors; it is translated as printed.

english: snakes fortify his head, and
note: muniant: concessive subjunctive with quamvis.

english: a foul breath and gore flows
note: manet: from mano, 'flows'; singular with the double subject.

english: from his three-tongued mouth;
Nay, even Ixion and Tityos with a face
note: quin et: 'nay, even'. Ixion and Tityos: sinners punished in the underworld.

english: unwilling smiled; the urn stood a little
note: risit: singular with the double subject. voltu invito: with unwilling expression.

english: dry, while with pleasing, Danaus' girls,
note: grato agrees with carmine (line 24). Danai puellas: the Danaids.

english: song you soothe.
Let Lyde hear the crime and the well-known
punishments of the maidens, and the empty of water
note: inane lymphae: 'empty of water', agreeing with dolium (line 27).

english: jar, through the lowest bottom perishing,
note: pereuntis: genitive with lymphae, 'water vanishing through the bottom'. fundo imo: ablative.

english: and the late fates
note: sera fata: the tardy punishments.

latin: quae manent culpas etiam sub Orco.
english: which await crimes even beneath Orcus.
note: Orco: Orcus, the underworld.

english: Impious, (for what greater could they?)
note: potuere = potuerunt: could they (do).

english: impious, their bridegrooms they were able with hard
note: 'their' supplied.

english: to destroy, iron.
note: duro ferro: with hard iron, i.e. the sword.

english: One out of many, of the marriage torch
worthy, toward her perjured parent was
note: in parentem: toward her father Danaus, who had broken his oath. 'her' supplied.

latin: splendide mendax et in omne virgo
english: splendidly lying and into all a maiden
note: splendide mendax: gloriously false. in omne ... aevum spans lines 35-36. virgo: Hypermestra.

english: renowned, time,
'Rise,' who said to her young husband,
note: The quotation marks render those of the source (Hypermestra's speech, lines 37-52). Order kept: quae dixit, 'who said'. 'her' supplied.

english: 'rise, lest a long sleep to you from where
note: longus somnus: death (metaphor). unde: from a quarter whence.

latin: non times detur; socerum et scelestas
english: you do not fear be given; the father-in-law and the wicked
note: detur: present subjunctive in the purpose clause.

english: sisters elude,
note: falle: deceive, escape the notice of.

english: who, like lionesses having got calves,
note: nactae: having caught.

english: one by one, alas, tear: I, than them
note: illis: ablative of comparison with mollior (line 43).

latin: mollior nec te feriam neque intra
english: softer, neither shall strike you nor within
note: nec ... neque: negatives kept.

english: bars shall hold.
note: claustra: bars, an enclosure.

english: Me let my father load with cruel chains,
note: 'my' supplied. oneret: jussive subjunctive.

english: because, merciful, I spared my wretched husband,
note: 'my' supplied.

latin: me vel extremos Numidarum in agros
english: me even to the farthest fields of the Numidians
with a fleet let him banish:
note: releget: jussive subjunctive.

latin: i pedes quo te rapiunt et aurae,
english: go where your feet carry you and the breezes,
note: pedes: your feet; 'your' supplied.

latin: dum favet nox et Venus, i secundo
english: while night and Venus favour, go with a favourable
note: favet: singular with the double subject.

english: omen, and, mindful of us, on a tomb
note: nostri: genitive of nos, 'of me'. memorem agrees with querelam (line 52): a mindful lament. sepulcro: dative/ablative, on my tomb.

english: carve a lament.'
note: The closing quotation mark renders that of the source.

latin: Miserarum est neque amori dare ludum neque dulci
english: It is of wretched girls neither to give play to love nor with sweet
note: Miserarum est: it is the lot of wretched girls. The speaker is Neobule (or the poet addressing her); the Latin gives no marker. neque ... neque: kept.

latin: mala vino lavere, aut exanimari metuentis
english: wine to wash away troubles, or to be terrified, fearing
note: lavere = lavare. mala: ills. metuentis: accusative plural, agreeing with the girls, 'fearing'.

english: the lashes of an uncle's tongue.
note: patruae linguae: a paternal uncle's tongue; verbera: lashes (metaphor for scolding).

latin: tibi qualum Cythereae puer ales, tibi telas
english: From you the basket the winged boy of Cytherea, from you the webs
note: tibi: dative of separation with aufert (line 5). qualum: wool-basket. puer ales: Cupid; Cythereae: of Venus.

english: and the zeal of industrious Minerva takes away, Neobule,
note: operosae Minervae: Minerva as goddess of weaving.

english: the radiance of Liparean Hebrus,
note: nitor Hebri: Hebrus' good looks, the second subject of aufert; Liparaei: from Lipara.

latin: simul unctos Tiberinis umeros lavit in undis,
english: as soon as his anointed shoulders he has bathed in Tiber waves,
note: 'his' supplied. lavit: perfect (or present, from lavo).

latin: eques ipso melior Bellerophonte, neque pugno
english: a horseman better than Bellerophon himself, neither in boxing
note: pugno: ablative of pugnus, 'with the fist'; neque ... neque: kept.

english: nor by slow foot defeated,

latin: catus idem per apertum fugientis agitato
english: shrewd likewise, through the open, the fleeing, with stirred
note: idem: the same man. fugientis agrees with cervos (line 11). agitato grege: ablative absolute.

latin: grege cervos iaculari et celer arto latitantem
english: herd, deer to spear, and quick in a close, lurking
note: iaculari: to hit with a javelin. arto agrees with fruticeto (line 12).

english: thicket, to intercept the boar.
note: excipere: to catch (the boar's rush).

english: O spring of Bandusia, more brilliant than glass,
note: Bandusia: a spring, probably on Horace's Sabine farm.

latin: dulci digne mero non sine floribus,
english: worthy of sweet unmixed wine, not without flowers,
note: mero: neat wine, offered in libation. non sine: kept.

english: tomorrow you will be presented with a kid,
note: donaberis: you will be presented (in sacrifice) with.

english: whose forehead, swelling with horns

latin: primis et venerem et proelia destinat;
english: first, both love and battles destines;
note: venerem: love, mating (lower-case in the source). primis agrees with cornibus.

english: in vain: for the cold, it will stain for you,
note: gelidos agrees with rivos (line 7); tibi: dative, 'your streams'.

english: with red blood, streams,
the offspring of the wanton flock.
note: suboles: subject of inficiet.

english: You the fierce hour of the blazing Dog-star
note: Caniculae: the Dog-star, Sirius, of high summer.

english: does not know how to touch; you a lovely cold
note: amabile: lovable, pleasant.

english: to bulls wearied by the ploughshare
offer, and to the wandering flock.
You will become, you too, one of the famous springs
note: fies nobilium fontium: partitive genitive, 'one of the noble springs'.

english: with me telling of the holm-oak set upon the hollow
note: me dicente: ablative absolute.

english: rocks, from where talkative
note: loquaces: chattering (metaphor).

english: your waters leap down.
note: lymphae: waters.
